en: Contrary to the belief that Filipinos executed him, Jose Rizal was actually killed by a firing squad of Spanish soldiers on December 30, 1896.
Although widely celebrated on June 12 now, the Philippines originally observed Independence Day on July 4 to commemorate the 1946 American recognition.
Despite the popular belief that the rare waling-waling is the national flower, the Philippine national flower is actually the white sampaguita.
Many mistakenly think the common maya is the national bird, but the official national bird of the Philippines is the critically endangered Philippine eagle.
Contrary to the idea that the President solely chooses the Chief Justice, appointees are actually nominated by the Judicial and Bar Council.
Unlike the common misconception that Igorot is a single tribe, it is actually an umbrella term for several distinct ethnolinguistic groups in the Cordilleras.
Although many believe Spanish remains an official language, the 1987 Constitution actually designates only Filipino and English as the official languages of the Philippines.
Contrary to the belief that she just studied medicine, Dr. Fe del Mundo actually invented a bamboo incubator for rural areas without electricity.
Contrary to the belief that Andres Bonifacio was the Katipunan's first president, Deodato Arellano actually served as its initial supreme president.
Unlike agricultural festivals that celebrate harvests, Cebu's Sinulog festival is actually a religious and cultural tribute to the Santo Niño.
Despite old laws requiring voters to be 21, the current Philippine Constitution actually lowers the voting age to 18 years old.
Contrary to the narrow belief that bayanihan only means carrying a nipa hut, it actually represents the broader Filipino value of communal cooperation.
